source_refs.note: Topic 2.3.5 Expressions as printed, with its Class Activity box (PDF 40, printed 37).

blocks.text: An expression is a combination of variables, operators, and values that produces a result. For example, 3 + 4 is an expression that results in 7. More complex expressions can use parentheses O to control the order of operations. For example:

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: "parentheses O" is a print slip for parentheses ( ), the brackets used in the example below.

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Write a program to calculate Body Mass Index (BMI). Ask the user for their weight and height, then compute and display their BMI and classification. The Body Mass Index (BMI) is calculated using the formula given below.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The formula is printed as BMI = weight / height. Body Mass Index divides the weight by the square of the height: BMI = weight / height², with weight in kg and height in m (in Python: weight / height ** 2).
